entry_conditions: Use the demonstrated red-first, then blue order with both named object poses and goals causally observed in the fixed world frame. The model receives two observations containing qpos/qvel, TCP and both object wxyz poses and goals; positions and finger coordinates are metres and arm coordinates are radians. The numerical API has no caller role-ID input, so roles are learned from these observations and an external nomination must agree with the supported order. Initial entry is supported at arm qpos approximately [0,-0.3,0,-2.1,0,1.8,0.7854], fingers 0.04 m each, TCP z=0.442 m and blocks z=0.02 m. Recurrent entry includes requested blue still at its source and predecessor red held over its own pad, descending around z=0.126-0.253 m with fingers about 0.0183 m each; do not treat this as an already disengaged predecessor. Internal shared pickup-overlap states include open low approach, closure and partially completed lifts. The model uses both object-goal nodes, TCP-object geometry, aperture and causal motion, not an elapsed-time trigger.
exit_conditions: Usual observed exit support is the requested block and TCP moving together near z=0.279-0.282 m, approximately preserved TCP-object pose offset, fingers about 0.01824-0.01830 m each (about 0.03653 m total aperture), and initial horizontal transport toward the requested object's own goal. Demonstrated targets continue gripper command -1. In demo10000 the TCP is roughly 9.5 mm in negative world X relative to held red and roughly 8.6 mm in negative world X relative to held blue; these are examples, not universal tolerances. Require qualitative relative-motion support rather than width or height alone. A proposed broader z=0.25-0.31 m or per-finger 0.015-0.025 m band is uncalibrated and not enforced. Exit here is a skill handoff cue, not the two-block task-success test.
overlap_role: The full expanded model is trained to complete predecessor goal-aligned lowering, hold the arm while opening, leave red on its pad, rise with open fingers and travel toward blue before acquiring blue. The role graph can nominate blue while still retaining red as predecessor and immediate manipulation context. It also learns the shared following-delivery overlap: low approach with fingers open, closing at object height, lift and first closed-gripper transport. Demo10000/265,300,350,400,424 and demo10003/255,290,335,408 show the former; demo10000/80,100,110,150,170,184 and /470,504,506,550,570,584 show the latter. Current object-goal error and height, TCP-object offsets, arm/finger state and short causal differences distinguish the transitions without a preset schedule. A contained predecessor at table height may still be inside nearly closed fingers, so a single geometric placement predicate does not describe transition readiness.
successor_readiness: Provide delivery with the same externally tracked requested-object name and its own goal, both live object poses, TCP pose, qpos/qvel and recent observations. At the usual elevated transfer it should preserve the observed grasp offset, continuing closed-gripper targets and ongoing horizontal motion rather than resetting to a canonical joint pose. Delivery may start earlier in the shared low-approach/closure/lift overlap if it can finish acquisition. The acquire model has no privileged contact memory, exported role cache or recurrent phase state to pass. Requested-object co-motion and a stable offset are only grasp evidence, not measured contact. The goal association must stay fixed even if the caller changes policy.
failure_signatures: Wrong role binding may move toward blue while red remains held, disturb already placed red, or close while TCP-object XY error is large. Rising TCP with requested-object z still near 0.02 m is evidence of a missed acquisition. Changing TCP-object offset despite narrow fingers suggests slip; narrow measured aperture alone cannot prove contact. A predecessor near its goal but still above the table and co-moving with TCP has not been disengaged. An external request contrary to the model's learned red-first order, unobserved/mislabeled object-goal pairing, or inconsistent nomination at transfer is an interface failure even if targets remain smooth. These observations should prompt API reassessment, not a claimed automatic recovery branch.
continuation_guidance: Reobserve after short action prefixes under the fixed horizon-16, execute-8 diffusion recipe. Continue this policy through residual predecessor lowering/opening/retreat and through supported requested-object approach, closing and lift until the successor can use the actual live state. The learned denoiser, not this text or the training-only role teacher, generates every low-level target. Do not switch merely because red is geometrically over its goal, a finger command has changed, or TCP alone has reached transport height. Conversely no additional mandatory dwell, zero-speed condition or canonical posture is required for the observed elevated handoff. Both policies can act inside the assigned shared overlaps; invocation duration is chosen by the inference API rather than an event index. When the full task placement contract holds, extra release, clearance or sustained-hold conditions must not be added as success requirements.
limitations: This is an executable learned-role adaptation of the original caller-supplied-role proposal because the fixed 47-channel interface lacks role IDs. No reversed-order acquisition, arbitrary external nomination, recovery from misses, obstacles, relocated bases or general goal transfer is established. Geometric role pseudo-labels are valid for these source slices, not a general contact or task-completion classifier. All measured boundary ranges and cited transitions are successful-demonstration support, not hard applicability cutoffs, calibrated handoff thresholds or policy performance measurements. Only two causal observations are available; dwell states and identical short histories may be ambiguous. There are no IK/FK constraints, contact sensor, persistent phase model or scripted recovery controller. The fixed shared whole-demonstration normalization is retained. Task success remains exactly red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal under the supplied rotated-containment and Z-tolerance contract.
